reasons.explanation: A defining field of the record being named is empty or absent, so its identity cannot be computed.
Two ports of one direction share a port_id, so the defining content is ambiguous.
A collection of names that must not repeat contains the same name twice.
Two nodes, two constants or two edges of the flow graph are the same member.
A text value of the defining content cannot be encoded as UTF-8; the kernel never repairs or normalizes text.
The byte content to be named is larger than the release ceiling for it.
The requested entity kind is not one the kernel mints identities for.
The kernel could not obtain safe entropy, and it never falls back to time, a label or request data.

properties.resource_bounds_never_exceed_release: each ResourceBounds field <= matching ReleaseCeilings field
properties.retention_uses_longest_reference: retention(value) = max(retention(record) for record naming value)

A22 rule 18 as amended on 20 September: a deep-module refusal names one closed code and one closed reason, and the response carries the catalogue's fixed explanation because the caller is an agent. Codes are the domain-originated subset of the public HTTP catalogue; authentication refusals stay unexplained under A21 and A27. Each module adds the reasons it owns as its State 7 notes are written.
